definition: Showing good judgment and an ability to notice subtle differences.
example: A discerning listener hears the tension beneath a polite reply.
nuance: Discernment implies judgment, not merely sharp eyesight.
prompt: An editor is choosing which essays to publish.
options: The discerning editor distinguished an original argument from a merely fashionable one.
The discerning editor accepted every essay without reading it.
The discerning editor could not tell an argument from an anecdote.
The discerning editor printed the essays in alphabetical order.
reasons: Careful discrimination between quality and appearance shows good judgment.
Accepting everything without examination shows no discrimination.
Failing to notice an important distinction is the opposite of discernment.
Alphabetical organization says nothing about judgment.
